title: React Suspense
description: Use React Suspense with React Query to declaratively handle loading states.

data.text: React Suspense lets components **declare** their loading state instead of manually checking `isLoading` or `isFetching`. With React Query, enabling `suspense: true` makes queries throw a special promise while loading, which Suspense catches and renders a fallback for. The result is cleaner component code and a single, declarative loading boundary.

terms.definition: A <Suspense> component that wraps loading components and displays a fallback while they fetch data.
A useQuery option that enables Suspense mode, causing the hook to suspend the component while loading.
The internal mechanism React Query uses to suspend â€” it throws a promise that Suspense recognises and catches.
The React element displayed inside a Suspense boundary while wrapped components are loading.

data.text: You can enable Suspense globally on the `QueryClient` or per-query by passing `suspense: true` in the query options. Enabling it globally is more common in production apps â€” it removes the need to set the option on every individual query.

data.title: QueryClient with Global Suspense Enabled
data.content: Configuring the QueryClient to enable Suspense mode by default for all queries.

data.title: Suspense Boundaries Are Hierarchical
data.text: Place Suspense boundaries at the route or section level. A nested boundary can show a skeleton for a specific widget while the rest of the page is already visible.

When Suspense is not enabled globally, you can opt individual queries into it. This is useful when migrating an existing app â€” enable Suspense on one feature at a time instead of switching over the entire app at once.

data.title: Per-Query Suspense Option
data.content: Enabling Suspense on a single query without changing global defaults.

data.text: When using Suspense, a failed query throws an error instead of setting `isError = true`. Wrap Suspense boundaries in an error boundary to catch thrown errors. This means you need both a Suspense boundary (for loading) and an error boundary (for failures) around any Suspense-enabled component.

data.title: Suspense Changes Error Handling
data.text: In Suspense mode, errors are thrown rather than set on the mutation object. You need an error boundary to catch them. isError and error will not be available inside a Suspending component.

data.title: Suspense Mode vs Manual Loading Checks

cards.title: Manual Loading
cards.description: Check isLoading and isFetching flags in every component.
pros: No error boundary required for data errors
cons: Mixed loading and data code in one place

cards.title: Suspense Mode
cards.description: Declarative loading â€” declare what should show while loading.
pros: Loading state is declared, not scattered
cons: Errors are thrown, not caught in-component
Not supported in all React versions

data.title: Good Candidates for Suspense
items: Page-level data fetching where a skeleton is a natural loading pattern
React Server Components â€” Suspense is required there
Shared loading logic across many routes â€” one boundary instead of many checks
New projects or features being built from scratch

data.title: Exercise: Migrate a Query to Suspense
data.description: Convert an existing useQuery component from manual loading checks to Suspense mode.
steps: Find an existing useQuery in your app that shows isLoading and isFetching.
Add suspense: true to the useQuery options.
Remove the isLoading check and any conditional rendering based on it.
Wrap the component in a <Suspense> boundary with a relevant fallback.
Add an error boundary above the Suspense boundary to catch thrown errors.
Verify the loading and error states still work correctly.
data.expectedOutcome: The component no longer needs isLoading checks. The Suspense boundary shows a fallback while loading, and the error boundary catches failures. The component body is simplified to only render data.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Suspense mode uses suspense: true to make queries throw a promise while loading
Wrap Suspense-enabled components in <Suspense> boundaries with fallbacks
Enable Suspense globally via defaultOptions or per-query
Errors in Suspense mode are thrown â€” use error boundaries to catch them
Suspense simplifies component code by removing manual isLoading checks
data.takeaway: Suspense + React Query is a powerful combination for production apps. Declare your loading states once, and let React handle the rest.
